analysis:
The changed files are docs/architecture/hardware-support.md and docs/architecture/inference.md. The PR adds a documentation section, "Pipeline decode command buffers", to inference.md, a summary paragraph at hardware-support.md lines 56-70, and "Last updated" bumps. No executable code, wire protocol, key handling, attestation, authorization, encryption, or coordinator-contract changes are included, so none of the TB-002, TB-003, TB-009, TB-011 or TB-012 controls are touched in this diff.

The documentation describes decode-step memory charging (QwenResidentPrefillTransient, Gemma4PrefillTransient, GPTOSSRequestStateBudget) and notes that the LOAD quotes and activation floors are unchanged. It also says GLM needs no added decode term and that GPT-OSS vector-kernel float32 partials beyond the priced rows are not charged, estimated at tens of MiB per request multiplied by the lanes. This is an availability and memory-accounting statement. It is labelled [INFERENCE] and is not a security regression in the supplied evidence.

I considered whether the uncharged excess is a DoS concern (T-029, A-018). It is small and is not shown to bypass the process-wide ledger or the OS headroom checks. The text states that live native/OS gates remain authoritative. The underlying source changes, such as QwenLayerStageSession.decodeCommandBuffers and the budget derivations, are not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot verify that the code matches the documented behavior. A later pass that sees those source files should confirm the documented charges. No data-exposure, prefix-cache (T-041) or at-rest artifact changes appear here.

The cross-repository agreement is that platform admission is unchanged, as the doc states. This claim is unverified here, but it is a documentation contract and not evidence of a defect.
